body:
`*` is a default mapping. `noremap = false` means you have enabled recursive mapping. Try `noremap = true`.

(We should name that option `remap` or `recursive`...)

But the claim is that this is a regression from 0.9.1, so if that is the issue, it shouldn't have worked before either. @lourenci can you verify this? Bisecting to which commit exactly changed the behavior would be helpful (if not necessary).

> (We should name that option remap or recursive...)

That's why we changed it for `vim.keymap.set` ;)

> We should name that option remap

I agree a 100% on that.

> Try noremap = true

I did it already. The result for the keymap is slightly different: it replaces with gn text.

What we want is: select this visual, get back to the previous result and change it keeping in insert mode (`cgn`). The result of this is that we can dot-repeat the next result with the typed one.

Let's stick to the actual issue reported here, which is the _regression_ of behavior for the _same_ command. We can talk about what you want to achieve and how in a different (feature request) issue or discussion.

Then why is ~~noremap=true~~ noremap=false  part of the repro steps? That is a useless complication.

in vim 9.0.1424 i see the same behavior with:

    vnoremap x *Ncgn

But the repro steps have `noremap=false`...

To be very clear: the only thing I care about in this issue is the 

> This is not an issue on stable.

part.

issue.title: fix(defaults): don't use nvim_feedkeys in default mappings

labels.description: Nvim defaults for options, colorscheme/theme, autocmds/events, etc.

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
Problem:    Using `nvim_feedkeys` in default mappings makes it hard to use
            them as a part of another mapping.
Solution:   Use an expression mapping and stop Visual mode later.

Fix #24518.
